newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr squeezes higher, key rate week looms.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr squeezes higher, key rate week looms.

text.p: The Australian dollar reached its highest level in a week as it broke through resistance on short covering, with comments from a former Reserve Bank of Australia governor ahead of a key data next week also helping.

After a soft start, the dollar posted gains from mid-morning until it was pressing against resistance at US$0.7380. After some volatility at this level, which had capped the dollar in offshore trade on Thursday, the unit broke higher.
By 4.45 p.m. (0645 GMT), the dollar was at US$0.7390/95, having reached a week high of US$0.7399, from an early US$0.7349/54 and Thursday's close of US$0.7365/70.

The dollar was already gaining strength when former RBA Governor Bernie Fraser, speaking in Melbourne, said the opportunity for a fifth rate cut had been missed. He said that whether one could still be delivered remained to be seen.

Steve North, head of foreign exchange at Chase, said Fraser's comment helped the afternoon rally a bit. "...But there was also a bank around here that had been selling Aussie all morning long, and he's taken back his short position."
As well, there had been some end-of-week short covering from others adding support to the market, North said.

The squeeze higher came ahead of a week when wages and inflation data are expected to add to the case for a local interest rate cut, a factor which has weighed on the dollar and sent it to an 18-month low of US$0.7310 earlier this week.
A sustained break above resistance would see US$0.7430 targetted as next resistance, and reverse some of the negative sentiment that currently surrounds the dollar, traders said.
Despite Fraser's comments, the market is still expecting a rate cut to follow in next week's second quarter inflation and wages data next Wednesday and Thursday.
"It was after the wages data the RBA moved last time, so clearly everyone will be looking for it next Friday if it's a benign number there," North said.

The consumer price index (CPI) next Wednesday is forecast to be negative 0.1 percent in the June quarter, the first negative outcome since the June 1992 quarter, according to median expectations of a Reuters survey of 27 economists. The annual rate is expected to be 0.5 percent, a 4-1/2 year low.
The key underlying rate, the focus of RBA policy, is epxected to drop to 1.7 percent in annual terms.
Not only would this be below the RBA's two to three percent target band, it would be the lowest rate since the series began in the early 1970's.

On Thursday, data is expected to show a 0.8 percent rise in average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE), the lowest quarterly wages growth in over one year. This would see annual growth moderate to 4.1 percent below the 4.5 percent level seen as the RBA's speed limit on wages.
That combination would be bullish for those looking for a rate cut, and negative for the dollar. If no cut is delivered, analysts said the dollar could bounce to US$0.7500.
The unit was firmer on the crosses, ending at 57.1 in trade weighted terms from an early 56.8 and a Thursday close of 57.0.
Against the yen, the dollar ended at 85.44/54 yen, up on an early 85.14/24 but still slightly down on Thursday's 85.56/66.
The big mover in the region was the New Zealand dollar, which dropped over a cent in early trade to a 19 month low of US$0.6467 on heavy selling, before closing at US$0.65.

Traders said the Kiwi selling was of the order of A$400 million, but apart from some buying of Australian versus New Zealand dollars, there was little direct impact on the local unit. -- John Mair 61-2 9373 1800
